the ALFALFA survey has detected 10,119 H I galaxies with 6 < log (M_(H I)/M_☭) < 11, and the H I mass functions of the 40% and 100% samples are in excellent agreement, and that we have measured Ω_(HI) to be 4.3 h^(–1)_70 ×10^(–5), 16% higher than the HIPASS value, and M* to be 1
the ALFALFA survey has produced the most accurate measurement of the H I mass functions to date and that the H I mass density is larger than the previous best estimate.

(1) the H I mass functions of the ALFALFA survey and of HIPASS are in agreement with each other, with Ω_(HI) ~ 4 × 10^(−4)h^(–1) and M* ~ 10^(9.9) M_☉, and (2) the Schechter function fit to ALFALFA data predicts an order of magnitute more galaxies than HIPAS.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ALFALFA survey has provided a robust and statistically accurate measurement of the H I mass functions of galaxies, which are in good agreement with the predictions of the ΛCDM paradigm, but with a few surprises.
we have now measured the H I mass functions to a level of precision sufficient to resolve the long-standing question of the discrepancy between baryonic and dark matter mass functions.
the H I mass functions from the 40% and 100% ALFALMA surveys are consistent with one another and with the Schechter function fit to the 40% sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ALFALFA has produced a large sample of galaxies that is well suited for measuring the H I mass functions and for constraining the baryon fraction in the local universe.

the H I mass distribution is well described by a Schechter function with parameters consistent with previous measurements, that the 2DSWLM method is a viable alternative for calculating H I mass functions, and that the 40% complete ALFALFA sample is an excellent data set for future studies of H I-selected systems.
the ALFALFA H I mass function is consistent with the predictions of ΛCDM and that the baryon fraction in the H I-selected galaxy population is 0.9 ± 0.1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H I mass functions from ALFALFA and HIPASS are in good agreement with one another and with the dark matter mass functions from the Millennium Run.
the mass function of galaxies with well-measured masses is in excellent agreement with the dark matter mass function.
the H I mass and volume density of the universe are larger than previously thought.
